Status: CLOSED — debrief appended at Review, 2026-07-16

The wave is complete; the DEBRIEF section at the bottom closes the story. Dated correction (2026-07-16, Review): this heading still read VERIFYING after the Decide phase appended D20–D32 and the wave plan — Decide omitted the status flip. The phase sections below are otherwise accurate in sequence.

The wish (verbatim)

Yes — (user approval of the proposed next wave:) W2 of the Scaffy epic: bp scaffy validate / bp scaffy fmt as Go code under internal/, implementing the D3+D12 grammar as code with the merged W1 corpus (scaffy/commands/*.scaffy) as the fixture set. The hand-apply test pass (2026-07-16, 6 agents) is the opening spec input: fix task-5901b9eff006f553 (add-oban-worker sibling accretion corrupts config.exs — REPLACE must re-anchor at the planted mark/current tail; matcher semantics must be pinned) and task-3e8ab72ce035abde (pin the 6 grammar semantics: REPLACE matcher rules, payload newline/indentation verbatim rule, CREATE mkdir -p, empty-fence bytes, opaque-literal vs snake-spelling contradiction, undeclared Pascal<->snake name transforms + hyphen-slug echo-vs-transform; plus the 5 prose fixes incl. the tsc assert's pnpm install && pnpm build precondition). The validator must ratify-or-reject the wave-log's new-by-example spellings: unplantable MARKs (docs-pair INDEX sweep), REMOVE with consumed mark, DELETE FILE IF PRESENT, ASSERT FILE EXISTS|ABSENT, positive-polarity ASLONG on remove ops, CountBefore/CountAfter +1 lint, and enforce the Ts 14-digit shape (D16). Validate/fmt only — no run/remove engine (that is W3).

Strategic direction

The finished experience: bp scaffy validate scaffy/commands/ reads like a compiler you trust — every .scaffy file parsed into a typed AST, every violation reported as file:line: RULE-ID message with a fix hint; bp scaffy fmt canonicalizes a command to the Review-unified spellings and is idempotent (fmt of fmt = identity, and the committed corpus is a fixpoint). The D3(a–g) + D12(A1–A5) grammar stops being prose and becomes executable law; the W1 corpus is both the proof (all 7 files validate green after the spec fixes) and the regression net (op census pinned: 11 CREATE, 5 INSERT AFTER FIRST, 1 AFTER LAST, 5 REPLACE, 1 REMOVE, 1 DELETE, 12 MARKs, 30 ASSERT FILE, 14 ASSERT CMD), plus one adversarial red fixture per lint rule — never a vacuous green.

Spec before code. The wave opens by settling the spec the parser will freeze: (1) task-5901b9eff006f553 — the add-oban-worker sibling-accretion bug: the crontab REPLACE must re-anchor at the planted mark / current tail so a second worker lands after the first with correct commas, and REPLACE matcher semantics get pinned (exact-line vs substring, comma/whitespace handling) so the behavior is engine-independent; (2) task-3e8ab72ce035abde — the 6 grammar semantics pinned in scaffy/README.md (matcher, payload newline/indentation verbatim rule, CREATE implies mkdir -p, empty-fence byte count, opaque-literal vs snake-spelling contradiction, name-transform declaration incl. hyphen-slug echo-vs-transform) + the 5 prose fixes (tsc assert precondition cd js && pnpm install && pnpm build; stale pdrender cites; fresh-Ts duplicate-body warning; add-cli-verb append wording + provenance; add-plugin discovery cite). The validator encodes exactly the pinned semantics — one truth, two renderings (README prose, Go code).

Ratify-or-reject, explicitly. Every new-by-example spelling from the W1 wave log gets a ruling recorded at Decide: unplantable MARK (docs-pair INDEX sweep — payload literal is the handle), REMOVE with consumed mark, DELETE FILE IF PRESENT, ASSERT FILE EXISTS|ABSENT, positive-polarity ASLONG on remove ops, CountBefore/CountAfter declared pair with the validator linting the +1. Lean: ratify all six as first-class grammar, giving unplantable MARK an explicit spelling rather than leaving it implicit. Plus the D16 Ts 14-digit shape as a variable-shape rule.

Tentative shape (Decide finalizes after two explore rounds): package internal/scaffy/ (lexer, AST, parser, lint catalog with stable rule ids, fmt printer), thin CLI wiring following the house pattern for local verbs; validator is pure text-level (no repo mutation, no network) — whether an optional repo-aware anchor check (--repo) is in scope is a survey question; AST anticipates W3 (marks as remove handles) without building any engine. Quality bar is Kinsta/Vercel: error output, help text, and README grammar reference all feel like a polished dev tool, not a school project.

House realities: the primary checkout is behind origin — the corpus exists on origin/main only, so all reading/building happens against origin/main in worktrees; Go-lane PRs merge on their own gates (no Elixir wait) but guerrilla auto-deploys internal/** merges, so merged = live bp binary; refresh local bp after CLI-touching merges.

Survey plan (16 scouts, in flight)

  1. corpus-census — verbatim read of all 7 .scaffy files on origin/main; complete statement/keyword/fence/variable census. Why: the parser's token set must cover 100% of the corpus.
  2. grammar-contradictions — every prose-vs-example contradiction in corpus + README (the 6 semantics and any others). Why: validator encodes one truth.
  3. oban-accretion — paper-reproduce the double-apply corruption; map the re-anchor-at-mark fix precisely. Why: settles task-5901b9eff006f553 + pins REPLACE matcher.
  4. cli-verb-wiring — how native local bp verbs register (builtins.go, cli.go); precedent for a no-server verb; -o json conventions. Why: scaffy validate/fmt must follow the house pattern.
  5. go-parser-prior-art — existing lexer/parser/AST idioms in internal/ (manifest, template, caddyfile, pdrender). Why: reuse over invention.
  6. fixture-harness — testdata/ + golden-file test precedent in internal/. Why: corpus-as-fixtures + fmt idempotency tests.
  7. new-spellings-inventory — quote every occurrence of the six new-by-example spellings in full context. Why: ratify-or-reject needs exact texts.
  8. mark-semantics — map all 12 MARKs: name, planted-by-payload text, op; does the review law hold everywhere? Why: MARK is idempotency now and the W3 remove handle later.
  9. variable-transforms — every VARIABLE declaration + token use; classify transforms, opaque literals, ambiguities. Why: the caser must be deterministic.
  10. ts-shape — the D16 Ts rule and the duplicate-body re-run warning in add-migration. Why: shape validator + prose fix.
  11. prose-fix-cites — verify all 5 prose-fix claims against live origin/main code. Why: fixes must cite live truth.
  12. bp-scaffy-namespace — verb-name collision check; builtin-vs-manifest resolution. Why: claim the namespace safely.
  13. fmt-scope — formatting variance across the 7 files; the diff a canonicalizer would produce. Why: decide fmt aggressiveness (fixpoint vs rewrite).
  14. backlog-and-papers — read scaffy-backlog-w2-validator and siblings + masterplan/showcase/W1 papers for validator requirements already decided. Why: don't re-decide settled things.
  15. lint-catalog — draft the exhaustive rule catalog from D3+D12+wave-log; classify text-level vs repo-aware. Why: scopes the validator honestly.
  16. merge-lane — which CI fires on internal/**; auto-deploy implications; bp freshness after merge. Why: builders need the gate spine.

Ledger links

Epic: bp-scaffy-epic (wave_status + wave_paper stamped). Opening spec inputs: task-5901b9eff006f553, task-3e8ab72ce035abde. Backlog riding this wave: scaffy-backlog-w2-validator; adjacent backlog that may get rulings: scaffy-backlog-elixir-local-gate-proof, scaffy-backlog-anchors-omx-exclusion. Charter: .claude/workflows/bp-scaffy-charter.md (D1–D19; W2 row in Roadmap).

Survey digest (Digest phase, 2026-07-16)

Established — settled ground truth, do not re-survey

  • Op census CONFIRMED twice independently, exact match to the charter: 11 CREATE / 5 INSERT AFTER FIRST / 1 AFTER LAST / 5 REPLACE / 1 REMOVE / 1 DELETE / 12 MARK / 30 ASSERT FILE / 14 ASSERT CMD (6 TIER ci). Freeze these as fixture-test assertions.
  • Correction to the wish's framing: ASSERT FILE ... EXISTS is NOT new — it shipped in W1 (add-plugin.scaffy:197, paired with the empty-fence .gitkeep). Only ABSENT (remove-docs-card.scaffy:91) is genuinely new. Decide ratifies them as two spellings, not one debuting pair.
  • MARK map complete: 12 declarations = 10 unique names; the docs pair intentionally reuses 2 names (claude-route-*, index-cards-*) as add/remove handle pairs — so a uniqueness lint must be direction/pair-scoped, never global. One mark (index-cards-*) is never planted (no comment syntax survives a brace expansion; the payload literal is the handle) — the corpus documents this honestly. 2 of 12 planted marks are not asserted in postconditions (js-count, cli-verb — deliberate semantic substitution); needs a posture ruling (hard lint vs allowed substitution).
  • Oban accretion bug root-caused and hand-traced across three candidate matcher semantics: (a) exact-whole-line → run 2 fails clean (anchor no longer matches, tool useless for siblings); (b) substring-match-consume-whole-line → the recorded corruption (two comma-less adjacent tuples, config.exs SyntaxError); (c) byte-exact splice (replace only fenced bytes) → survives N runs but silently reverse-orders workers and breaks the corpus's own unique-anchor invariant + charter A4's intent. Charter A4 already decided the DIRECTION (run ≥2 anchors at the planted mark) but no grammar syntax exists to express it — the fix is a new primitive (mark-family anchor selector or first-run/subsequent-run branch), a Decide-level ratification. Same defect class exists in add-cli-verb (its own comment at :70-72 claims mark re-anchoring the op cannot express). add-block-type's CountBefore/CountAfter is the working counter-pattern (caller re-supplies current state per run).
  • Ten prose-vs-example contradictions cataloged with file:line evidence, including two NOT named in either opening task: (i) the corpus carries two unreconciled solutions to the moving-target REPLACE problem (parameterize-state works, static-literal breaks); (ii) MARK has a second, undeclared meaning (nominal handle with no in-file bytes). Both are structural, not editorial.
  • Opaque/pair/shape are ONE decision, not three: the opaque-literal contradiction (ColumnType/Summary/PathTemplate spelled snake while declared no-transform), the CountBefore/CountAfter +1 pair, and the Ts 14-digit shape all live only in DESCRIPTION prose today. All three need the same ruling: does VARIABLE gain an annotation syntax (OPAQUE / SHAPE / PAIR) or does the validator hardcode names? Recommended caser model: one word-list tokenizer (treating _, -, and case boundaries as equivalent separators) + four joiners, with OPAQUE as a structural flag.
  • CLI wiring is a solved house pattern: case "scaffy": in cli.go's Execute() switch (runs BEFORE manifest load — builtins shadow manifest nouns), pure-local like make/style (never call resolveContext/loadManifest → structurally zero server dependency), verb tests co-located in package cli. "scaffy" must be added to completionNouns (builtins.go:316-323) or TestCompletionNounsCoverAllDispatchedBuiltins reds. Namespace is clean both directions (no CLI case, no manifest noun, no plugin named scaffy). Open: exit code for lint findings — exitValidation(5) exists but no local builtin uses it yet.
  • No parser prior art halves the build. internal/manifest + internal/template are JSON decoders; internal/caddyfile is a writer (good fmt donor: determinism, splice-safety guards); pdrender/mermaid.go is the ONE line-oriented text parser but its doctrine (silently skip unparseable lines) must be INVERTED, not copied. No position-carrying error type (ParseError{File,Line,Rule}) exists anywhere in internal/ — file:line machinery is new work. Best synthesis: mermaid.go's line-scan shape + manifest.Tree's byName index + template.Validate's deterministic errors + caddyfile's printer idioms.
  • Fixture harness settled: tests read the corpus IN PLACE via relative path ("../../scaffy/commands" — exact precedent: internal/manifest + internal/cli reading ../../docs/cli/fixtures). NO go:embed in W2 (embed cannot leave the package dir; the sync+drift-tripwire pattern exists at internal/provisioner/catalog if W3+ ever needs it). fmt fixpoint (bytes.Equal(Fmt(Fmt(x)),Fmt(x))) is NEW test vocabulary — no repo idiom exists.
  • fmt scope should be narrow: the corpus is already at a fixpoint on every grammar-structural dimension (header field order, VARIABLE shape, blank lines, section order, op-clause order, zero trailing whitespace; tabs only inside the Go payload where they are verbatim content). Sole substantive divergence: add-cli-verb's generic fence labels (target/payload vs descriptive everywhere else) + its all-caps POSTCONDITIONS heading — a NEW finding, absent from the 6+5 lists. Recommendation: fmt canonicalizes grammar tokens only, never comment prose.
  • Merge lane, verified against workflow YAML: go-tests.yml (blocking) and doc-gates.yml (blocking — it fires on **/*.go too, not just .md) gate W2's PRs; elixir.yml runs on EVERY PR (no paths filter — the older memory note is wrong) but blocks nothing since main has zero branch protection; deploy.yml auto-deploys guerrilla on internal/** merges (merged = live bp) with no YAML-visible human gate; bare .scaffy files trip nothing. W1 dodged CI; W2 is genuinely gated.
  • House reality is STRONGER than the direction stated: the primary checkout is not merely behind — it sits on a foreign branch (loop-epic/prove-portabledoc-…). The scaffy corpus and internal/scaffy work exist only relative to origin/main. All building happens in worktrees off origin/main; surveyors read via git show origin/main:… (all did).
  • Backlog alignment: scaffy-backlog-w2-validator's acceptance criteria (corpus green + 4 seeded legacy red fixtures + fmt idempotency + Go gate) match this direction exactly. The masterplan's roadmap groups parser+engine as one step; W2's validate/fmt-only scope is a deliberate narrowing — record at Decide so it reads as intent, not drift. Until scaffy-backlog-elixir-local-gate-proof closes, the validator treats every Elixir ASSERT CMD as TIER ci-only per A2.

What Decide cannot live without (the decision stack)

  1. REPLACE matcher + scope pin — recommended: byte-exact match on the exact fenced bytes, replace ONLY those bytes — plus the ratified spelling for run-≥2 re-anchoring (mark-family selector vs first/subsequent branch vs sentinel-INSERT redesign). This decides the oban fix AND the add-cli-verb comment fix.
  2. VARIABLE annotation syntax (OPAQUE / SHAPE / PAIR) vs name-hardcoding — one ruling unlocks three lint rules.
  3. Unplantable-MARK spelling + validator default posture (error unless the explicit spelling is present, vs silent tolerance).
  4. Empty-fence byte semantics (0 bytes vs one newline) — binds both fmt and the EXISTS assert.
  5. --repo mode in or out of W2 — anchor-existence/occurrence checks (W-101/102/103/105) are the one rule class pure text validate cannot cover; the corpus's own "grep -cF = 1" claims stay tool-unverified for two waves if deferred.
  6. Exit-code scheme (exitValidation=5 for findings vs exitGeneric) and fmt rule set (fence-label rule in/out; comment prose untouched).
  7. Lint granularity for the remove-direction trio — unplantable MARK / consumed-mark REMOVE / positive-polarity ASLONG are three faces of one op-direction rule family; one composable rule beats three fragmenting IDs.
  8. SNIPPET/USE synthetic fixture — the grammar rule has ZERO corpus instances; per never-vacuous-green doctrine it needs an authored fixture or an explicit deferral.

Coverage map — checked and NOT found (absences are decisions-in-waiting)

  • internal/scaffy/: does not exist anywhere, local or origin — fully greenfield (proven via find + git ls-tree).
  • SNIPPET/USE: zero instances in the 7-file corpus (README says so itself).
  • No CI workflow references scaffy/ at all; bare .scaffy diffs trip nothing.
  • No position-carrying parse-error type and no format-fixpoint test idiom anywhere in internal/.
  • scaffy absent from CLI builtins, completionNouns, live manifest (21 nouns), and plugin names.
  • D3(g)'s URL-position casing clause: vacuous against the corpus (zero real fixtures exercise it).
  • README grammar reference: zero hits for mkdir / newline / indent / REMOVE / DELETE FILE / EXISTS / ABSENT / positive ASLONG / CountBefore-After (grep-proven) — all six new-by-example spellings are corpus-only law today.
  • Corners NO surveyor reached: scaffy/showcase/*.json unopened; internal/cli/builtins.go helpers only inferred from call sites; GitHub 'production' environment protection rules (outside workflow YAML) unknown; the ~8 stale .claude/worktrees/wf_*/scaffy copies never diffed against origin/main; full byte-diff of every code-citation RANGE in the corpus (anchors verified, ranges spot-checked); Barkpark full-text search never successfully invoked (the CLI has no bp search verb — real endpoint is search.query) so org-wide prior art beyond charter/tasks/papers is unswept.

Verify plan (6 assignments, in flight)

  1. oban-matcher-proof (opus) — mechanically apply add-oban-worker's crontab REPLACE twice (workers Foo, Bar) to origin/main's config.exs under all three matcher semantics; PROVE each outcome by parsing every result with elixir -e 'Code.string_to_quoted!(…)'. Turns the hand-trace into run output; pins the matcher recommendation with evidence.
  2. tsc-precondition-proof (sonnet, worktree) — in a fresh worktree at origin/main, RUN cd js/packages/react && npx tsc --noEmit (expect the false red), then cd js && pnpm install && pnpm build, then tsc again (expect green). Proves the exact precondition spelling the prose fix will pin.
  3. greenfield-harness-proof (sonnet, worktree) — throwaway internal/scaffy/probe_test.go reading ../../scaffy/commands/*.scaffy by relative path, re-deriving the op census programmatically; RUN CC=clang go build ./... && go vet ./internal/scaffy/... && go test ./internal/scaffy/... plus go test -run TestCompletionNounsCoverAllDispatchedBuiltins ./internal/cli/. Proves the fixture-read pattern, the census, a greenfield package under the real gate, and the completion tripwire — before any real code is written.
  4. corpus-lint-dry-run (opus) — implement the core text lints (token 4-spelling closure, guard-payload derivation, mark-required, guard polarity, path snake-casing, fence pairing) as a throwaway script and RUN it over all 7 files; report the exact green/red matrix and exception list (expected: index-cards unplantable mark; cli-verb id-guard). Decide gets a proven default-posture list, not prose.
  5. deploy-human-gate-check (sonnet) — gh api the repo's 'production' environment protection rules and main branch protection (expect 404). Closes the one auto-deploy unknown the YAML cannot show.
  6. prior-art-and-hygiene-sweep (sonnet) — resolve and RUN the real search invocation (search.query) over papers+tasks for scaffy prior art; confirm the charter's tracked state on origin/main; diff every stale worktree scaffy copy against origin/main to prove no divergent corpus edits are floating.

Verification results (2026-07-16 — the deep round, all six assignments returned with run-proofs)

  • oban-matcher-proof — PROVEN, all three forks reproduced by parser. Exact-whole-line: run 2 fails clean (RUN2_ERROR: VARIANT-A NO MATCH) — accretion impossible. Substring-consume-whole-line: reproduces the recorded corruption verbatim — ** (SyntaxError) invalid syntax found on nofile:255:8: error: syntax error before: '{'. Byte-exact splice: parses across 3 runs but lands workers NEWEST-FIRST (Baz, Bar, Foo) and never uses the mark. The recommended pin — byte-exact match + MARK-scoped re-anchor — was then proven directly: Foo→Bar→Baz→Foo-rerun yields FORWARD order, parses, guard keeps the re-run a no-op (Foo count = 1). Critical trap found: a naive "last Workers.X tuple" tail-finder grabs the pre-existing non-scaffy TagDistribution tuple at config.exs:232 — the planted mark line is the ONLY safe re-anchor key. Not found: any parser donor (git show origin/main:internal/scaffy → path does not exist).
  • tsc-precondition-proof — CONFIRMED with a bonus. Fresh worktree: tsc reds with 103 errors, exit 2 (no node_modules at all, not merely core's dist). cd js && pnpm install && pnpm build → 11/11 turbo tasks, then the identical tsc exits 0 (twice). BONUS: the adjacent vitest assert (line 298) shares the root cause and the same cure — 12 files / 192 tests green. One preceding ASSERT CMD fixes both. Not found: any pnpm-precondition precedent anywhere in the corpus — a genuinely new spelling.
  • greenfield-harness-proof — ALL FOUR CLAIMS PROVEN. Greenfield internal/scaffy builds/vets/tests clean under CC=clang; the relative-path fixture read (../../scaffy/commands, manifest pattern) works; the op census re-derived by machine matches 11/5/1/5/1/1/12/30/14 exactly; TestCompletionNounsCoverAllDispatchedBuiltins passes pre-change and WILL red an unwired noun. Load-bearing gotcha: without CC=clang the internal/cli test build fails on cgo (error: unknown option '-E') — every gate command must thread it.
  • corpus-lint-dry-run — CORPUS IS LINT-CLEAN; two RULES were mis-specified. 6-rule dry-run over all 7 files: single red = {{.Ts}} Pascal-in-path (the opaque-literal fork). "Snake-only in paths" is WRONG — it reds the correct kebab docs paths; the true rule is lowercase-only. Guard polarity is textually UNDECIDABLE (the containment heuristic false-positived on remove-docs-card's correct un-sweep swap) — direction must be declared, never inferred. E-006 must exempt whole-file CREATE/DELETE. Confirmed: cli-verb id-guard is payload-derived (green); MARK:index-cards appears nowhere (the unplantable mark is real).
  • deploy-human-gate-check — ZERO human gate, proven at every level. gh api …/environments/production → {"deployment_branch_policy":null,"protection_rules":[]}; all 6 environments identical; branch protection 404 ("Branch not protected"); rulesets []. Merged internal/** = LIVE bp on guerrilla, no checkpoint.
  • prior-art-and-hygiene-sweep — clean search, one REAL hazard. search.query for "scaffy": 22 hits, all inside the known universe — no surprise prior art. Charter tracked on origin/main and byte-identical to the working copy (diff exit 0); the checkout is a FOREIGN branch (4 ahead / 26 behind), which is why the file reads untracked locally. HAZARD: 3 of 21 stale .claude/worktrees scaffy copies DIVERGE from canon (pre-review squash-merge leftovers: old MARK spelling, old positive-ASLONG polarity, old fence labels) — backlogged as scaffy-backlog-stale-worktree-drift; builders must never glob worktrees.

Decisions (charter D20–D32, committed to origin/main)

  • D20 — REPLACE matcher = byte-exact fenced-bytes, replace only those bytes. The only variant that both fails safe and composes; the other two forks were proven to dead-end or corrupt.
  • D21 — REANCHOR "<mark-prefix>" is first-class REPLACE syntax. Run ≥2 anchors at the LAST planted mark block of the family; proven to give forward order + parse + guard-idempotency. add-oban-worker AND add-cli-verb (same defect class) gain it. Self-consuming REPLACE without ASLONG + REANCHOR = lint error.
  • D22 — VARIABLE annotations become grammar: OPAQUE, SHAPE "ts14", SUCCESSOR "Name". ONE ruling resolves the opaque-literal contradiction, the Ts 14-digit shape (D16), and the CountBefore/CountAfter +1 lint — the wish framed these as three items; they are one syntax decision.
  • D23 — DIRECTION "add"|"remove" required header field. Polarity is textually undecidable (proven); the remove trio (positive ASLONG, consumed marks, ASSERT ABSENT) is ONE direction-driven rule family.
  • D24 — Unplantable MARK ratified as MARK VIRTUAL. Plain MARK must plant its text in its own payload (the lint that would have caught W1's one real bug); VIRTUAL requires an ASLONG. Mark uniqueness pair-scoped.
  • D25 — New-by-example spellings RATIFIED (REMOVE, DELETE FILE IF PRESENT + required distinguishing guard, ASSERT EXISTS|ABSENT — correction: EXISTS predates the wave-log; only ABSENT debuts). SNIPPET/USE stays, synthetic fixtures only.
  • D26 — Payload bytes verbatim; empty fence = 0-byte file; CREATE implies mkdir -p (engine prose, not a W2 lint).
  • D27 — validate is pure text; --repo CUT to backlog. Exit codes 0/5/2/4; fmt in-place + --check; fmt never rewrites comments/payloads; generic fence labels = WARN.
  • D28 — Lint catalog corrected by dry-run: E-009 lowercase-only-in-path (not snake-only); E-006 fenced-ops-only.
  • D29 — one new ASSERT CMD "cd js && pnpm install && pnpm build" before the tsc assert — cures tsc AND vitest. Census: ASSERT CMD 14→15.
  • D30 — Post-fix census frozen: 11/5/1/5/1/1/12 (2 VIRTUAL)/30/15 (6 ci); corpus read in place via ../../scaffy/commands; adversarial red fixture per rule; dedicated conformance test lands last.
  • D31 — CLI shape: builtin switch + completionNouns, pure-local (make/style pattern), doctor-style per-format report, CC=clang on every gate.
  • D32 — House realities binding: foreign-branch checkout (read canon via git show origin/main:), never glob worktrees, merged = live (zero human gate).

Wave plan (4 slices, integration-ordered — tasks published under bp-scaffy-epic)

#tasksurfacemodelfilesgate
1scaffy-w2-grammar-lawspec — README + corpus encode D20–D26/D29 + 5 prose fixes; closes task-5901b9eff006f553 + task-3e8ab72ce035abdefablescaffy/README.md, scaffy/commands/check-doc-budgets.sh + census greps (ASSERT CMD=15, REANCHOR×2, DIRECTION×7, MARK VIRTUAL×2)
2scaffy-w2-core-packageinternal/scaffy — lexer + AST + parser (file:line findings) + lint catalog + fmt, synthetic green/red fixtures (no corpus reads)fableinternal/scaffy/CC=clang go build ./... && vet && test ./internal/scaffy/...
3scaffy-w2-cli-wiringbp scaffy validate|fmt — pure-local builtin, exit codes 0/5/2/4, -o json, polished help; AFTER slice 2 mergesopusinternal/cli/, docs/cards/cli.mdCC=clang go build ./... && vet && test ./internal/cli/... (incl. completion tripwire)
4scaffy-w2-corpus-conformancecorpus green + D30 census freeze + fmt fixpoint over the committed corpus; AFTER slices 1+2 mergeopusinternal/scaffy/corpus_test.goCC=clang go test ./internal/scaffy/ -run 'TestCorpus.*' -v

Backlog filed this wave: scaffy-backlog-w3-engine (run/remove engine + Oban runtime smoke), scaffy-backlog-repo-aware-validate (--repo anchor checks, cut by D27), scaffy-backlog-stale-worktree-drift (3 divergent stale copies), scaffy-backlog-js-assert-sweep (fresh-checkout false-red sweep beyond add-block-type). scaffy-backlog-w2-validator is superseded by slices 2–4 (lead closes with the wave). Builders fly next; Review closes this story as the debrief.

DEBRIEF — Review, 2026-07-16 (wave closed, grade A-)

What shipped

1. scaffy-w2-grammar-law — final branch loop-epic/scaffy-grammar-law-readme-corpus-encode--0 (clean at review; no fixes needed). README gained the “Wave-2 rulings — D20–D26, the validator’s law” section; all 7 corpus files carry DIRECTION; REANCHOR on add-oban-worker + add-cli-verb (closes task-5901b9eff006f553); D22 annotations applied (Ts OPAQUE SHAPE "ts14", 10 OPAQUE literals, CountAfter SUCCESSOR); both INDEX sweeps are MARK VIRTUAL; the D29 pnpm-bootstrap ASSERT CMD landed; all 5 prose fixes carry live-verified cites (closes task-3e8ab72ce035abde). Review re-proofs: D30 census exact (11/5/1/5/1/1/12(2V)/30/15(6ci)); both REPLACE anchors (ticket.close map, PlaygroundReaper tuple) occur exactly once in the live tree; docs-anchors-check.sh green (the builder had skipped it); gate re-run green.

2. scaffy-w2-core-package — final branch loop-epic/internal-scaffy-greenfield-lexer-typed-a-1-r (the review branch — merge THIS, not the original). Greenfield internal/scaffy: fail-loud parser, typed AST with positions, frozen 28-rule catalog, idempotent structural fmt, 28 adversarial red fixtures with exact RULE-ID+line expectations. The builder worked blind of the corpus by design, and the designed tripwire FIRED at review: running the live grammar-law corpus through the package produced 198 findings from three spelling divergences (one-line header with TAGS comma-list + trailing VARIABLES; EXAMPLES comma-lists; CREATE … WITH) plus two lint-scope bugs (E-006 ignored guard polarity — the remove-direction un-sweep guard legitimately derives from the TARGET; E-012 bound its ASCII rule to ASSERT CMD shell strings the ratified corpus carries em-dash caveats in). Review fixed all five in place on the -r branch, added a regression test pinning the corpus spellings, and proved the endgame: all 7 corpus files ValidateFile ⇒ zero findings AND are fmt fixpoints. Full gate green after fixes.

What stalled, and why

scaffy-w2-cli-wiring and scaffy-w2-corpus-conformance were never built: both are sequenced “AFTER <sibling> merges” but were dispatched in the same parallel round as their unmerged dependency. Structural, not a timing fluke — builders don’t push and the lead merges only at review, so a same-round sequenced slice can never gate. Both tasks hold honest BLOCKED now-lines with ready-to-apply survey handoffs. Dispatcher lesson: a slice whose brief says “AFTER X merges” belongs in a second round.

Ledger audit

Clean. All four slice tasks in_progress with criteria stamped mid-work and merge-gated criteria honestly open; the two blocked tasks record their stalls in now-lines; task-5901b9eff006f553 + task-3e8ab72ce035abde stamped met with evidence, left for the lead to close on merge. One fix applied: the epic task’s criterion 0 (Wave 1 shipped) was still unstamped despite W1 having merged and the showcase being live — stamped at review with evidence.

Grade: A-

What earns it: the grammar-law slice is genuinely excellent — every cite re-verified live, census exact, and the REANCHOR/VIRTUAL/OPAQUE encodings read as one coherent law across README and corpus. The core package is well-architected (fail-loud doctrine, positions everywhere, frozen catalog, adversarial fixtures) and its blind-build risk was contained exactly as designed. What holds it from A: the parser shipped diverging from the normative corpus on three spellings a single corpus read would have caught — review absorbed a fix the conformance slice was designed to catch later, and half the wave (CLI + conformance) never built due to a dispatch-shape error, so the wish’s visible surface (bp scaffy validate as a command) does not exist yet.

Next wave

(1) Lead merges the two final branches (grammar-law original, core -r) and closes the merge-gated criteria + the two spec tasks + scaffy-backlog-w2-validator; refresh local bp. (2) Re-dispatch cli-wiring and corpus-conformance — both near-mechanical now (corpus validation + fmt fixpoint pre-proven at review). (3) Then W3 engine (bp scaffy run/remove): pin the REANCHOR family-extent rule for multi-line marked blocks (add-cli-verb’s 18-line map) — the one semantics D21 left to the engine.
